t: Automatic Folder Organizer: a plain-language overview
title: Automatic Folder Organizer: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Automatic Folder Organizer does and why archives need it. An automatic folder organizer puts every loose file where it belongs. You give it rules — 'invoices go in Finance', 'photos go in Media' — and it files everything, even thousands of files at once. Before it moves anything for real, it shows you a dry run so you can check its work.
demo:
# Automatic Folder Organizer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK171-000001)
import re
RANK = 1
SIG = False
FILES = ['invoice_march.pdf', 'photo1.jpg', 'notes.txt', 'app.py', 'scan.png']
RULES = [(r"\.pdf$", "Documents"), (r"\.(jpg|png)$", "Media"), (r"invoice", "Finance"), (r"\.(py|js)$", "Code")]
plan, quarantine = [], []
for f in FILES:
    dest = next((d for pat, d in RULES if re.search(pat, f, re.I)), None)
    (plan if dest else quarantine).append((f, dest))
print("filing plan (dry run):")
for f, d in plan: print("  %-22s -> %s" % (f, d))
for f, _ in quarantine: print("  %-22s -> QUARANTINE (no rule)" % f)
if RANK >= 2:
    print("filed:", len(plan), "| quarantined:", len(quarantine))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("destination histogram:", dict(Counter(d for _, d in plan)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-FLD-" + "JAH-ATK171-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK171-000001", "OK")

t: How the Automatic Folder Organizer works: the deep tour
title: How the Automatic Folder Organizer works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Automatic Folder Organizer does and why archives need it. Real organizers combine rule engines (extension, filename pattern, date, size, sender) with content classifiers that read a file's text or metadata to choose its folder. Conflicts — two rules claiming one file — resolve by rule priority, and every action is logged with its reason. A dry-run mode previews all moves, and an undo journal reverses a whole run if the rules were wrong. Scheduled sweeps keep watched folders perpetually tidy. Advanced organizers learn rules from a user's past filing behavior, quarantine files that match no rule instead of guessing, and detect rule drift when filing patterns change. Quality is measured by filing accuracy on a held-out set of human-filed documents and by quarantine rate. The limits are genuinely ambiguous files and personal naming schemes the rules never saw — those wait in review with the organizer's best guess attached, never filed blind.

import re
RANK = 3
SIG = False
FILES = ['budget.pdf', 'pic2.png', 'readme.txt', 'tool.py', 'mystery.xyz']
RULES = [(r"\.pdf$", "Documents"), (r"\.(jpg|png)$", "Media"), (r"invoice", "Finance"), (r"\.(py|js)$", "Code")]
plan, quarantine = [], []
for f in FILES:
    dest = next((d for pat, d in RULES if re.search(pat, f, re.I)), None)
    (plan if dest else quarantine).append((f, dest))
print("filing plan (dry run):")
for f, d in plan: print("  %-22s -> %s" % (f, d))
for f, _ in quarantine: print("  %-22s -> QUARANTINE (no rule)" % f)
if RANK >= 2:
    print("filed:", len(plan), "| quarantined:", len(quarantine))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("destination histogram:", dict(Counter(d for _, d in plan)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-FLD-" + "JAH-ATK171-000015")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK171-000015", "OK")
